changelog: Fix: a full run of the parser against challenge 6's real Position History read all 59 positions correctly, but 32 came back 'needs attention' purely on entry_price precision (e.g. LIT 4.6370 vs stored 4.6300, INJ 5.321 vs stored 5.3200) -- the same hand-transcription precision gap already fixed for pnl in v3.14.4 applies to entry_price too. BitfundedImportController::matchAll() now compares entry_price with a relative tolerance (ABS(entry_price - incoming) <= 0.5% of the incoming price) instead of exact equality -- relative, not absolute, because this account's prices span 0.0044 to 71,968 and no single absolute tolerance is both loose enough for the low end and tight enough for the high end. The tolerance base is always the incoming Bitfunded price, never the stored value, so a stored 0.0000 (see next fix) can never make the tolerance permanently zero

Fix (live defect, independent of the importer): entry_price, exit_price, stop_loss, and take_profit were DECIMAL(14,4) -- four decimal places, which floors out inside this account's real price range. Three PUMPUSDT trades are stored with entry_price 0.0000 right now because the real price is a fraction of a cent, below what four decimal places can represent at all -- an outright loss of the value, not a rounding error, and it makes any R computed from a stop-loss on a low-priced pair meaningless. Migration 2026_09_18_0002 widens all four columns to DECIMAL(20,10), comfortably covering this account's full observed price range. Widening a DECIMAL's precision/scale is data-preserving -- no pre-flight guard needed -- but does not recover the three already-zeroed PUMPUSDT rows; that precision was lost at write time under the old column type and can only come back from a real re-import, which the 0.5% relative tolerance still won't auto-match for these three specifically (0.0000 vs the real price is a 100% difference, not a precision gap)
